rationales: Ecology studies relationships between organisms and their environment.
Morphology studies the form and structure of organisms.
Genetics studies heredity and variation.
Parasitology studies parasites and their relationships with hosts.
Chitin is a major component of fungal cell walls, not plant cell walls.
Cellulose is a major component of plant cell walls.
Cholesterol is a membrane lipid, not a major plant cell-wall component.
Glucose is a simple sugar and is not the principal structural material of plant cell walls.
Medicine concerns the prevention and treatment of disease.
Agriculture concerns crop production and farming more broadly.
Forestry concerns the management of forests.
Horticulture includes the art and science of gardening.
Xylem transports water and dissolved mineral substances through plants.
Phloem chiefly transports sugars and other organic substances.
Stomata are pores that regulate gas exchange and water loss.
Leaves are organs, not the plant tissue specialized for transporting water.
Melvin Calvin discovered the reactions now commonly called the Calvin cycle or dark reactions.
Karl Lohmann is associated with the discovery of ATP, not the dark reactions.
Koshland is not credited with discovering the dark reactions.
T. Schwann is known for contributions to cell theory, not the dark reactions.
Experiments test deductions rather than serving as their source.
Deductions or predictions are drawn from a hypothesis.
A theory is a broader explanatory framework, not the usual source of a specific deduction in the scientific method.
A law describes a regular pattern and is not the usual source of a specific deduction in the scientific method.
Tubulin forms microtubules, not microfilaments.
Tropomyosin associates with actin filaments but is not their main structural protein.
Myosin is a motor protein that interacts with microfilaments but does not form them.
Actin is the main protein forming microfilaments.
Parenchyma is a common cell type in plant ground tissue.
Vessel elements are components of xylem tissue.
Tracheids are components of xylem tissue.
Sieve tubes are components of phloem tissue.
Meiosis produces gametes and is not the usual process whose errors cause tumors.
Errors in the regulation of mitosis can cause uncontrolled cell division and tumors.
Binary fission is a form of prokaryotic cell division, not the process responsible for typical tumors.
Multiple fission is not the process whose errors cause typical tumors.
Apoptosis is programmed, regulated cell death rather than accidental cell death.
Regeneration is the replacement or regrowth of lost or damaged parts.
Necrosis is accidental, uncontrolled death of cells and tissues.
Fragmentation is a mode of reproduction or body division, not accidental cell death.
Amylase is used in some laundry detergents to break down starch-based stains on clothes.
Amylase is not commonly used as the key enzyme in dishwashing products.
Amylase breaks down starch and is not used for colouring.
Saponification is soap formation by reacting fats with alkali, not a use of amylase.
The light reactions are not conventionally called the S-scheme.
The light reactions are not conventionally called the X-scheme.
The light reactions are not conventionally called the Y-scheme.
The sequence of electron transfers in the light reactions is represented by the Z-scheme.
Arteries generally carry blood away from the heart.
Capillaries connect arterioles and venules and allow exchange with tissues.
Arterioles carry blood away from the heart toward capillaries.
Veins carry blood toward the heart.
Viruses are not the microorganism used to produce insulin in this context.
Fungi are not the standard organisms used for recombinant insulin production.
Algae are not the standard organisms used for recombinant insulin production.
Genetically engineered bacteria can produce human insulin.
Jabir bin Hayan is known for work in chemistry, not authorship of Al-Qanun-Fi al-Tib.
Ali Ibne Eisa was an ophthalmologist, not the author of Al-Qanun-Fi al-Tib.
Bu Ali Sina (Avicenna) wrote Al-Qanun-Fi al-Tib.
Abdul Malik Asmai was a scholar of natural history and language, not the author of this medical encyclopedia.
